answer.text: Deactivating but ortho/para directing; the acyl group enters mainly para
answer.line: Bromine pulls electrons through the sigma bond and slows the ring, but its lone pair steers the newcomer ortho and para. Bulk picks para.

steps: Split the two effects. Induction: bromine pulls electron density out and slows every attack. Resonance: a bromine lone pair helps only the ortho and para attacks.
Induction decides the speed, so bromobenzene is deactivated. Resonance decides the place, so the group goes ortho or para.
The acylium ion is bulky, and ortho sits right beside the bromine. Para is open, so para is the main product.

choices.text: Activating and meta directing; the acyl group enters mainly meta
choices.note: Both halves run the other way: bromine slows the ring and directs ortho and para.

choices.text: Deactivating and ortho/para directing; the acyl group enters mainly ortho only
choices.note: The classification holds. But ortho sits next to bromine and the acylium is bulky, so para is the main product, not ortho.

choices.text: Deactivating but ortho/para directing; the acyl group enters mainly para
choices.note: Deactivating by induction, ortho/para by resonance, para by room.

choices.text: Deactivating and meta directing; the acyl group enters mainly meta
choices.note: Most deactivators do direct meta. Halogens are the one class that breaks that rule, because the lone pair still donates by resonance.

choices.text: Activating and ortho/para directing; the acyl group enters mainly para
choices.note: Direction and position hold. But ortho/para does not make bromine an activator; its pull still slows the ring.

lockIt: Halogens are deactivating by induction and ortho/para directing by resonance.
